summary: Full E2E testing of Confluence Decoder (Heatseeker GEX). All 9 backend pytest tests passed against live REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. Frontend renders correctly with SPY heatmap, spot line, patterns (Rug + Beach Ball), velocity gauge, structural nodes table, air pockets, and movers panel. Ticker buttons (SPY→QQQ→NVDA), mover clicks (INTC), and Trinity mode (3 panels with partial_alignment verdict at 67% confluence) all work. Filters (side/lifecycle/expiries/magMin) render and respond. JSON responses are NaN/Inf-safe. ^SPX works via URL-encoded %5ESPX.

issues: With 100+ strikes within ±15%, the center column becomes very tall and the right rail (patterns/velocity/nodes/air pockets) extends beyond the viewport requiring scroll. Acceptable for a dense GEX terminal, but consider virtualizing or capping rows for SPX (small-tick) tickers.

Velocity score shows 100 on initial loads because the snapshot delta is large after the first run; this is expected per agent_to_agent_context_note. May want a 'warming up' indicator for the first few snapshots.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py line 610: `ticker.upper().replace(...) if ticker.upper() in ('SPX',) else ticker` — non-SPX paths skip .upper(), so lowercase tickers like 'spy' fall through unmodified. Consider always `ticker.upper()` and a single normalization map (SPX -> ^SPX).

server.py velocity_and_rolling(): compares current strikes against the most recent snapshot, but build_heatmap saves the snapshot AFTER computing velocity — good. However, snapshot_count returned is `len(history) + 1` which double-counts the not-yet-saved current snapshot; cosmetic.

Frontend App.js line 602: `max={Math.abs(data?.nodes?.king?.gex||1e9)}` — when data is null, max defaults to 1e9 which makes step=1e7 reasonable, but optional chaining returns undefined first, so the `||1e9` triggers only on falsy. OK.
Backend has no /api/health endpoint; / works as a heartbeat (returns app/version/ts).
No data-testid coverage gap observed for tested flows; all interactive elements (ticker buttons, trinity-toggle, movers, custom-ticker-input, filter panel buttons, trinity panels/tiles) have testids.
test_credentials: N/A — app is read-only, no auth
seed_data_creation: Mongo snapshots auto-created by heatmap calls during testing (used for velocity comparison)
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend tests live in /app/backend/tests/test_heatseeker.py and pass against the public REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. yfinance fetches can take 5-15s on cold cache; tests use generous timeouts. ^SPX must be URL-encoded as %5ESPX. Trinity endpoint takes ~10-15s. Movers endpoint uses yfinance bulk (~5-8s) cached 60s. Velocity score may show 1.0 (=100 on UI) on early calls — expected, not a bug.
